# Bounded all-definition inventory

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — M3d adds source-backed candidates alongside
> upstream retained metadata, using the existing authenticated adapter,
> collection boundary and transactional protocol.

## What and why

`option-metadata` facet `all-definitions`, mode `metadata`, inventories one
exact requested option path. “All” covers bounded enumerable admitted module
bodies. It includes losing overrides and inactive leaf bindings without
traversing every config value or forcing inactive payloads. Existing
`nx_definitions` and `SelectedDefinition` still mean upstream retained inputs
before type merging and `apply`.

`ql/queries/LosingDefinitions.ql` returns exactly
`(target, contextPathJson, optionPathJson, candidateOrigin, candidatePriority, winningPriority, active, selected, wrapperChainJson)`.
Its Boolean columns are true and false respectively. It reports only active
candidates with a known effective override priority strictly greater than the
observed winner. Inactive and unknown candidates remain accessible through
`Modules::DefinitionCandidate` and extraction health, without a losing claim.
Order priorities never determine override losers. One shared signed-decimal
comparator in `internal/Evaluation.qll` preserves endpoint precision without QL
integer conversion.

## Integration and authority

The supervisor derives source plans in `src/eval/definitions.py` from admitted
exact bytes and authenticated S2 anchors. Literal option paths, nested attrsets,
explicit `config.<path>` bindings and literal merge lists are enumerable.
Helpers and lexical aliases must resolve through the existing pinned module
model. Closed wrapper records preserve outer-to-inner `if`, `merge`, `override`
and `order` structure and merge indexes. Ordinary leaves use a safe constructor
allowlist, including lexically unshadowed `true`/`false`/`null` and unary-minus
integer/float literals. Dotted locals, recursive bindings, function parameters
and inherit aliases retain shadowing; computed expressions and custom property
records are opaque.

`src/eval/nix/adapters/evalModules.nix` applies the existing module wrappers and
asks the pinned library's `modules.collectModules` for enabled unique-key
modules. Only collected source plans become evaluated candidates; unreachable,
disabled and duplicate occurrences do not add candidates. M3g still exposes its
separate occurrence graph. Collection transports plans in its unused config
field, never through value merging. A clean evaluation of the same pinned
library supplies the internal module's declaration identity; a matching
collection root preserves upstream key collisions without reserving user keys.
Internal `key == _file` equivalence is source-verified only for this pinned
library and must be checked again when its pin changes. The ordinary
argument-support root stays intact.

This uses a deprecated exported upstream collector. Its warning consumes the
supervisor's stderr-inclusive byte budget. A pin removing the API fails the
request rather than establishing empty completion. Do not add a parallel
collector to hide this dependency.

The adapter captures optional `unsafeGetAttrPos` points on original applied,
source-proven wrapper-free binding paths before sanitization reconstructs attrs.
Wrapped or opaque payloads are not traversed for runtime positions. Coordinates
identify bindings in UTF-8 bytes, not RHS causation; source snapshots still
authenticate files. Root-file library/formal bindings retain M3p's coverage and
are emitted on successful selection and inventory transactions. Missing library
descriptors or `specialArguments.lib` suppress helper-dependent candidates and
make the inventory partial.

`src/eval/nix/modules.nix` emits upstream retained definitions, `isDefined` and
winning priority in the same request as candidates. Candidate ordinals follow
enabled collection order, source byte order and merge-index order. Identity
frames request, option, collected module key, binding anchor and merge-group
path; it is distinct from retained-definition identity and ordinal.

The four added relations are `nx_candidates`,
`nx_definition_candidate_priorities`, `nx_definition_selections` and
`nx_observation_candidates`. `schema/contract.json` owns their types;
`schema/abi.py` validates admitted anchors, closed canonical wrappers, group
identity, contiguous ordinals, typed observations and same-request
correspondence. Each selected correspondence is unambiguous on both sides.
Positive correspondence requires one eligible authenticated source occurrence
and one retained record with its exact label; same-file ambiguity stays unknown.
A matching basename is insufficient.

## Boundaries and limits

Activity and selection are independent tri-states. A supported enclosing false
guard establishes inactive; enabled modules with all supported guards true
establish active. A guard hidden beneath order or override is unknown because
upstream discharge does not see through that barrier. False guarded leaf
payloads may stay unforced. Dynamic guard truth stays unknown. Effective
override priority is absent for unsupported nesting; source spelling alone
cannot select an override.

Known defect R3-LM1: an inactive opaque leaf without a visible override
currently receives ordinary priority `100`; the contract requires absent
priority. Safe literal leaves and visible override priorities remain valid. This
cannot produce a losing row because the candidate is inactive.

Selected false needs inactivity or a known worse effective override plus
winning-priority witness. Selected true needs authenticated retained
correspondence. Absence from retained files proves neither. An incomplete
inventory suppresses positive correspondence; it may still publish known
candidates and retained metadata.

Generated/unanchorable modules, dynamic keys or list spines, computed bodies and
free-floating `mkDefinition`/custom properties produce `partial` with
`definition-body-opaque`. Upstream may force an opaque config body before
metadata and fail; preserve that failure. Supporting arbitrary inactive bodies
or universal correspondence needs a separately approved evaluator
instrumentation contract.

`observedCount` and `maxNodes` count option + candidates + retained definitions;
wrappers are not nodes. Root-only `maxDepth=0` refuses any candidate or retained
child. Producer and supervisor both enforce this boundary. Existing byte, text,
time and memory limits still apply, and refusals publish no successful
transaction. Complete empty inventories need an observed option witness; missing
rows do not prove emptiness. Exact-pin capability checks apply to coordinated
real extraction. Trusted synthetic command fixtures test transport independently
of real producer/model support.

## Changes and validation

Extend the existing contract, validator, supervisor, source planner, adapter and
thin QL library together; preserve one collection authority and one decimal
comparator. Regenerate schema/model projections with existing generators.
Register notes in the owner registry and regenerate instruction projections with
`devenv tasks run --mode before generate:all`. Preserve independent
original-byte anchor expectations and upstream Nix oracles when extending
recognition.

Linux `codeql-nix-modules` runs
`checks/fixtures/inc3/all-definitions/test_all_definitions.py` for ABI,
transport, source admission, correspondence and budget refusal. Its domain
runner prints `test_all_definitions.py: N tests, N executed`. These synthetic
cases do not prove the production planner or installed QL.

On x86_64-linux, `codeql-nix-step0` runs `test_installed_all_definitions.py`
against the installed producer and queries, reviewed qltest rows and independent
`oracle.nix`. Look for `test_installed_all_definitions.py: N tests, N executed`
and evidence text
`M3d all-definitions with direct oracles and reviewed losing rows`. Cases cover
baseline/priority flip, ties/ambiguity, wrapper boundaries, opaque bodies,
disabled/duplicate closure, original UTF-8 points, helper suppression and signed
endpoints. `codeql-nix-abi`, `codeql-nix-contracts` and
`codeql-nix-raw-inventory` retain schema/import/transport/drift coverage. These
are registered checks and expected markers, not a claim that CI passed.

# Generated builtin identities

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — M3 derives builtin identities from the
> packaged runtime and its registration source, installs their model and
> activates the shared run fingerprint under one fixed evaluation policy.

## Terms

- Alias: another exported name for the same builtin identity.
- Builtin: a primitive exported by the pinned Nix runtime.
- Confidence: whether a record has recognized registration-source evidence.
- Evidence span: a source path and inclusive line range supporting metadata.
- Export: a name exposed globally or under `builtins`.
- Fingerprint: a content hash identifying the complete generated model.
- Identity: an opaque label for one builtin in one runtime/source pair.
- JSON: the structured data format used for the installed model asset.
- Model: versioned builtin facts derived from runtime and source inputs.
- Namespace: the export container; the empty string denotes global names.
- NAR hash: Nix's content hash of a directory tree.
- Opaque behavior: no claim about what invoking the primitive does.
- Oracle: an expected answer obtained independently of model generation.
- Parser: a program that recognizes grammatical structure in source text.
- Pin: a fixed input version or content identity.
- Policy: the fixed feature, purity and plugin settings for this model.
- QL: CodeQL's query language.
- Registration: C++ source that declares a runtime primitive or constant.
- Runtime: the packaged Nix executable used to enumerate exports.
- Sentinel: a competing test value used to reveal which name wins.
- Tree-sitter: the parsing library used to recognize C++ registrations.

## What is generated and why

`models/builtins/generate.py` reads the actual `builtins` export inventory from
the runtime under `models/builtins/policy.json`: exactly `flakes nix-command`,
pure evaluation and no plugins. The generator clears ambient Nix configuration
sources and search paths; the installed evaluator consumes that same policy in
its existing isolated invocation. The bundle covers this scope only, not
arbitrary user configurations. It probes candidate global names with competing
`with` sentinels, without invoking exported functions. Each inventory member
gets a distinct identity; observed global and namespace aliases share it. Names
missing from the inventory get no identity.

A tree-sitter C++ parser reads supported `RegisterPrimOp`, `addConstant` and
`addPrimOp` registration forms under the same runtime's `src/libexpr/`.
Recognized records retain argument names, literal documentation and evidence
spans with `source` confidence. Missing registration evidence yields `unknown`
confidence and null metadata. Unsupported or computed documentation remains null
even when other registration evidence exists. Every record keeps opaque
behavior; metadata proves no function summary.

The generator records its version, exact stripped `nix --version` output and
source NAR hash. The JSON also records the enforced policy. `modelVersion` is
`sha256:` plus the hash of compact, sorted-key UTF-8 JSON excluding that field.
This identifies content independently of display formatting.

`generated/models/builtins.json` is the sole model representation. The generated
`builtins.qll` is a mechanical projection of that JSON, not a second authored
inventory. Models add no evaluation tables or syntax rules.

## Installation and consumers

The existing `lib/packaging.nix` assembly supplies the runtime and its own `src`
together. It passes JSON through the shared generated-tree formatter and
preserves generated QL bytes. The library installs `models/builtins.json` and
`nix/internal/generated/Builtins.qll`.

Queries import `nix.internal.BuiltinModels`.
`builtinIdentity(namespace, name, identity)` exposes identities only when the
database's `nx_runs` model fingerprint matches the installed builtin/module
bundle, and that bundle's builtin fingerprint matches this model.
`runtimeIdentity`, `runtimeSourceHash` and `modelFingerprint` describe the
builtin model; `bundleIdentity` is the common bundle fingerprint this library
accepts as a run's model identity, and
[N2's runtime-globals frame](implicit-scope.md) requires exactly that of the run
before generated globals become definite targets; `supportsRuntime` checks
exactly its runtime/source pair within the fixed policy above. It does not test
arbitrary runtime settings. A different policy changes the complete model
fingerprint; a missing or mismatched model cannot establish builtin resolution.

The existing [shared run identity](installed-extractor.md) carries the common
bundle fingerprint: SHA-256 of canonical sorted compact JSON mapping `builtins`
and `modules` to their respective model fingerprints. The generated module model
records `bundleHash`; changing either model changes the run identity.
Builtin-only JSON generation and its own `modelVersion` remain independent.
[Target admission](target-contract.md) rejects an explicitly requested different
model. Legacy `not-requested` targets remain valid. Lexical binding resolution
and shadowing belong to the name resolver; import edges belong to the later
import domain. This module supplies identities for those consumers without
resolving source names itself. [N2](implicit-scope.md) wires generated globals
into the outer explicit frame. `globalBindingIdentity` exposes raw global
inventory only to reserve recognized spellings when fingerprints are absent or
incompatible; this does not establish compatible resolution. `builtinIdentity`
retains its fingerprint gate.

## Verification and changes

`checks.nix` imports `checks/builtin-models.nix`, exposing the Linux check
`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-builtin-models`. Its explicit nonempty Python
runner checks runtime inventory, alias uniqueness, source-backed `map` metadata,
opaque records, content fingerprints and shared run propagation. It regenerates
twice, applies the assembly's JSON formatter and compares committed and
installed bytes.

The same suite explicitly runs `NameBindings.ql` and `ModelCompatibility.ql`
against the installed extractor and library, using independent expected rows. A
real Nix oracle compares global and namespace `import`, competing sentinel
values and a safely renamed local binding. These checks establish the
builtin-identity part of names, rather than a complete lexical resolver.

To change generation, update the generator policy or runtime/source inputs
together, preserving the shared policy enforced by generation and installed
evaluation. Run
`python models/builtins/generate.py --nix NIX --source PINNED_NIX_SOURCE --output DIRECTORY`
from the owner directory, format the JSON through the assembly's treefmt policy,
and review both generated artifacts together. Never hand-edit the generated
inventory or projection. Preserve exact compatibility, explicit unknowns and
independent expectations; run the owner check through CI and update this note
when these obligations change.

# Handwritten database contract

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — M3g adds the module-graph closure: a module
> entity, five relation tables and native Booleans; F1 validates occurrence-tree
> structure, single-position occurrences, typed witnesses, observed counts,
> incomplete-closure atomicity and module-origin admission; M3d adds four
> candidate relations with authenticated correspondence.

## Purpose and ownership

`schema/contract.json` owns the version-one relation inventory, column types,
primary keys, enums and serialization encodings. `schema/abi.py` supplies
reference encoders and validates unordered fact collections. Its `dbscheme()`
renders the committed `schema/evaluation.dbscheme`; the ABI check rejects
divergence. All 36 handwritten relations are independent of generated AST entity
types, so later syntax and evaluation producers can contribute to one database
without manufacturing raw kit labels.

The [integration gate](integration-gate.md) records production lookup, text and
coordinate proofs after bootstrap retirement. F1 defines the shared ABI; later
producers and QL consumers preserve it rather than infer semantics from missing
rows.

## Durable identity

Global keys use `nixql:v1:<namespace>:` followed by
`<UTF-8-byte-length>:<component>` for each component. Namespace and component
boundaries distinguish equal-looking concatenations; empty components remain
present. No Unicode normalization, path resolution or worktree-prefix insertion
occurs in this encoder.

The frozen semantic components are:

- Root: logical name and root content identity.
- File: root key, root-relative path and file content digest. Absolute checkout
  locations are mapping data.
- Anchor: file key, decimal start byte, exclusive end byte, grammar kind and
  canonical ordered structural child-index path. Equal spans with different
  kinds or child paths remain distinct.
- Evaluation fingerprint: evaluator, lib, adapter and model versions;
  manifest-arguments hash; source-snapshot hash; policy hash; and system.
  Context, option-path segments, observation facet and occurrence distinctions
  must survive in the identities built on that fingerprint.

The validator reconstructs file and anchor keys and checks their components.
Candidate keys additionally check request, option, anchor and merge-group
components against their witnesses and wrapper chain. Other entity keys are
checked for namespace and framing, not reconstructed from their semantic inputs.
The component list freezes the producer obligation; accepting a well-framed
target key is not evidence that its fingerprint was computed correctly.

Option/request paths are compact canonical JSON arrays of exact string segments:
`["a.b"]` differs from `["a","b"]`. Contexts are root-only with instance path
`[]`; structural child paths contain nonnegative integer indexes. Canonical JSON
uses UTF-8 text, no optional whitespace and no ASCII-only escaping. Source paths
must be nonempty, relative and free of `..` segments; this lexical check does
not resolve symlinks or authenticate filesystem contents.

## Priority and exact text

Native relation integers are nonnegative and at most `2147483647`, rejecting
Python Booleans. Enum columns accept only the listed contract values. Unknown
optional information belongs in an absent auxiliary relation, rather than an
invented enum value or default false.

Option priority holds canonical signed decimal text over
`[-9223372036854775808,9223372036854775807]`. Zero is `0`; a nonzero magnitude
has no leading zero, plus sign or exponent. Negative override priorities are
valid. Consumers must retain decimal precision rather than narrow priorities to
a native QL integer. `priority-domain-unsupported` identifies an unsupported
range. An option priority also requires same-option `isDefined = true` metadata
and an observed `pre-apply-metadata` witness from an `option-metadata` request
with facet `all-definitions`, `priority` or `selection`, the exact option path
and context, and a `complete` or `partial` result. Step 0 itself used only the
`pre-apply-metadata` stage and the `option-metadata` domain. The sole option
metadata field is `isDefined`.

`nx_definition_order` optionally associates a retained definition with order
priority in the same exact decimal domain. It is separate from winning override
priority; absence establishes no default order. The retained definition and
parent option need observed witnesses under the same successful request.
`nx_module_lib_bindings` links successful selection and all-definitions requests
to admitted function/formal anchors, with library and model hashes matching
their target and run. The formal must belong structurally to that top-level
function; the adapter establishes the actual invocation and supplied library.
See [module-properties.md](module-properties.md) for its producer and consumer.

Every text column is limited to **1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes**, measured before TRAP
quote doubling. JSON payloads and path arrays are checked after JSON encoding,
including escaping expansion. Invalid UTF-8 and oversized fields raise
`ValueError`; no truncation or chunk protocol exists. Global key framing itself
is exempt; keys repeated in text columns still obey the ceiling.

A later producer must reject an oversized file/projection transaction and report
`text-field-too-large` using representable enclosing identities. It must publish
no clipped facts or successful observations from that transaction. F1 validates
facts supplied to it; it does not implement atomic publication, automatically
manufacture failure rows or preflight the generated syntax writer. The
[integration gate](integration-gate.md) documents production syntax preflight
and its owner-check evidence.

## Scope, admission and completeness

Primary keys are unique per relation, definition ordinals are unique per option,
foreign entities must exist with the declared type. `nx_observations` contains
only observation, request, stage and state. Every observation in every state has
exactly one subject row in total: `nx_observation_options(observation, option)`,
`nx_observation_definitions(observation, definition)`,
`nx_observation_contexts(observation, context)`,
`nx_observation_modules(observation, module)` or
`nx_observation_candidates(observation, candidate)`. All subject columns are
typed entity references; text subject kind/key columns are removed. Missing,
duplicate, wrong-type, dangling and simultaneous links of different kinds are
invalid. Context and module subjects must belong to their request's context and
to that context's single `module-graph`/`closure` request.

Requests belong to their context's target. The linked option, or a linked
definition's parent option, must belong to that exact context and hence target.
A request path need not equal its subject's option path except for the priority
witness above. Consumers must join typed subjects, rather than infer identity
from request paths or metadata presence. A definition observation identifies
only its linked definition, not every sibling definition of its option.

`nx_target_inputs` admits a file to the source snapshot of its target's run. For
origins used by declarations, definitions or modules, an `nx_origin_files` link
must have admission for every referencing run's snapshot. Admission is supplied
evidence: F1 neither hashes source bytes nor authenticates labels, roots or
symlink policy. Diagnostics link directly to requests and targets; no
diagnostic-origin relation is retained. File-level links do not establish
expression-to-value edges or unique syntax associations.

Every `observed` observation requires its own `complete` or `partial` request
result, `complete` only when the request's domain is `module-graph`. A
`module-graph` request that is not `complete` publishes no module rows for its
context, and a complete closure carries exactly one context witness plus exactly
one module witness per occurrence. Each module occurrence occupies exactly one
root or child position. Missing rows mean unknown. Completed definitions require
positive work and contiguous ordinals for the request's same-path/context
observed options.

The [bounded inventory](all-definitions.md) adds distinct candidate records,
optional effective priorities and unambiguous retained correspondences. F1
requires same-request option/candidate/definition witnesses and exact observed
counts on complete or partial inventory transactions; inactive or unknown
candidates do not manufacture retained rows.

A complete request cannot carry a timeout/text refusal reason or a linked
diagnostic with either code. Failed discovery can be represented before any
target exists. The validator checks these recorded consistency rules; it does
not prove that all phases/results were reported, that a budget was obeyed, that
a completion claim is true, or that all unobserved facts are false.

## Validation and changes

`checks/fixtures/abi/golden.py` supplies independent serialization expectations
and a graph covering every relation. `test_abi.py` checks identity,
enum/reference/scope rules, priority witnesses, refusal and UTF-8/JSON-expansion
boundaries. `checks/abi.nix` runs these tests, checks schema projection
equality, compiles against the standalone handwritten schema and imports/checks
typed golden TRAP. This does not prove production extraction.

Change the contract first, update validation and independent ABI/F2/supervisor
fixtures, regenerate `evaluation.dbscheme` through `dbscheme()` and the combined
schema through S1, then format affected files. Run the owner ABI, contracts, raw
inventory and evaluation-isolation checks through CI. Preserve typed-schema
import coverage, scope rejection tests and adversarial subject-link controls. An
ABI change requires full database regeneration; version one promises no in-place
upgrade or migration path.

## Deferred consumers

Remaining increment 3 cuts restore context-parent tables, nested contexts and
their scope validators. Increment 4 restores value/scalar/member/string-context
tables, encodings, value observations and their validators. Additional option
metadata fields return with their named consuming query; schema contexts are
dropped because increment 3 selects concrete instances only. The
diagnostic-origin relation is permanently dropped. These surfaces have no Step 0
producer or consumer.

# Evaluation isolation and projection publication

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — E1 implements the serialized projection
> boundary; E2a adds [module metadata](module-adapter.md); M3 shares the fixed
> builtin export policy with model generation; M3g adds the module-graph closure
> domain with supervisor-owned depth and node budgets.

## Purpose and fit

`src/eval/supervisor.py` accepts an F2 manifest, explicit opaque-reference
bindings and a TRAP destination through `supervise`. It launches one subprocess
at a time for each selected request. Failure in one request leaves completed
projections available. It does not discover flake outputs, enter a devenv shell
or select an adapter from its label. E2a reports module-adapter support. The F2
`option-metadata` domain supports `declarations`, `definitions`, `isDefined` and
`priority` facets at root depth (`maxDepth = 0`) in `metadata` mode. The
`module-graph` domain supports the `closure` facet over a whole-root context:
the supervisor recomputes import-tree depth and observed nodes from returned
edges, refuses atomically before publication when either budget is exceeded or
the returned closure is incomplete, and rejects a manifest admitting two graph
requests for one context, or a graph request outside the closure facet and empty
path, during discovery before any request runs, while structure, subject scope
and counts stay F1's to validate.

`src/eval/protocol.py` enables all three F2 custom formats and delegates exact
text, identity and fact validation to F1's `schema/abi.py`. Its TRAP renderer
uses F1 global labels and columns. Keep this shared authority: adding a second
relation validator or inferring success from empty output would violate the
[database](database-contract.md) and [target](target-contract.md) contracts.

## Runtime bindings and admission

The caller supplies a map resolving `evaluation.reference`, `moduleArgumentsRef`
and `specialArgumentsRef`; labels are never parsed as selectors. A binding
selects either an explicit `expression` path or a trusted fixture `command`.
Module and special arguments must be JSON representable. This boundary does not
transport arbitrary runtime functions or secret-bearing argument closures.

For a real expression, the supervisor resolves the path under a declared source
root, hashes each admitted root with Nix and imports a hash-pinned local
`fetchTree` copy. A separate admitted tree carries the request job. Roots are
admitted whole directories; this is not file-level snapshot authentication.
Descriptor identity and fingerprint strings are caller-supplied evidence, not
independently authenticated hashes of the copied roots.

A second declared root is accessible through its exact hash-pinned local
`fetchTree` URI. A projection may use this shape, with that root's actual path
and independently computed `nix hash path` result:

```nix
import ((builtins.fetchTree {
  narHash = "sha256-<root hash>";
  path = "/absolute/declared/dependency";
  type = "path";
}).outPath + "/value.nix")
```

Original absolute imports are not rewritten and remain blocked by pure
evaluation. E1 does not manufacture framework input handles. Each request gets a
disposable local Nix store and writable home/cache/temp directory. The
environment is rebuilt. The supervisor and [builtin model](builtin-models.md)
generator consume one fixed `models/builtins/policy.json`: `flakes nix-command`,
pure evaluation and no plugins. The supervisor applies these settings within its
existing isolated invocation. Nix also receives restricted evaluation, offline
operation, an allowlist of the exact pinned local tree URIs, no substitution, no
builders, `max-jobs = 0` and disabled import-from-derivation. No lock-update
command is invoked. These controls apply to Nix expression bindings; a trusted
command binding is a test transport and does not receive a network or filesystem
sandbox.

The Linux check supplies `pkgs.nix` (tested Nix 2.34.9) from the flake's locked
nixpkgs through `CODEQL_NIX_TEST_NIX`; production callers select the executable
through `supervise(..., nix=...)`. Changing that runtime requires rerunning the
real isolation cases. This slice makes no Darwin isolation claim.

## Budgets and transaction boundary

A request deadline covers root hashing and evaluation. Child processes get a new
process group, an address-space ceiling from `maxMemoryMiB` and disabled core
dumps. Both output pipes are drained, with their combined bytes bounded by
`maxBytes` (`byte-limit` on overflow). F1 separately enforces its per-field
1,048,576-byte ceiling (`text-field-too-large`); multiple legal fields may
exceed that size in aggregate. Timeout or excess output kills and reaps the
process group. Run diagnostics retain at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes of a message.

Accepted output must be one F2 envelope with exactly its request result. For
option metadata, options and observations must match the selected context, path
and request; metadata must match the requested facet. Every observation has
exactly one typed subject link, validated by F1. The supervisor accepts option
and definition subjects for option metadata, and context and module subjects for
graph closure. A complete projection observes each emitted option and
definition, or the context and each module occurrence, exactly once. Origins
belong to emitted definitions, declarations or modules, and positions belong to
those origins. Producers cannot emit supervisor facts. [E2a](module-adapter.md)
authenticates caller-admitted source links.

A complete option-metadata request requires a positive observed count and an
`observed` option witness for the selected facet. `isDefined` and `priority`
also require their respective metadata rows; declarations may be empty with an
observed option. F1 independently requires each priority's same-option
`isDefined = true` and priority-request observation. A result-only envelope,
unforced observation or missing metadata cannot establish success. The complete
graph passes F1 validation before publication. `maxNodes` bounds option,
definition, declaration, observation and reported counts. Child limits exclude
JSON/F1 validation and publication; the supervisor has no aggregate memory
ceiling.

Each validated projection is written to a temporary file, flushed and renamed to
a completed `.trap` file. An invalid transaction publishes no metadata.
Supervisor-owned run, phase, target, context, capability, request and diagnostic
rows are published separately at completion. This is a per-projection handoff,
not an atomic whole-run snapshot or a proof of crash recovery. Completed
transactions survive another request's error. Strict mode raises
`ExtractionFailed` after publishing status evidence, carrying the full validated
packet.

Missing bindings, denied paths, missing inputs and recognized evaluator refusals
are blocked; other producer errors fail. Targets and the evaluation phase expose
incomplete requests. Exception messages classify some Nix refusals, so changed
runtime wording requires checking the blocked/failed distinction. A malformed
manifest records failed discovery before any target is admitted. Missing
observations never imply absent options or completed metadata.

## Exact CI entry point and cases

`checks.nix` imports `checks/eval-isolation.nix`, exposing the Linux-only
`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-eval-isolation`. It runs
`checks/fixtures/eval-isolation/test_supervisor.py` through F3's explicit
nonempty domain runner. The runner reports each named test and its executed
count; `$out/evidence` is written only after the suite passes. No CodeQL engine
or database import runs in this check.

The fixture has two complementary oracle groups:

- Fake producers check bound arguments, literal target names and paths, statuses
  and completed-file handoff; serialized execution; error isolation with
  strict-mode evidence; crash/malformed/invalid/forged/foreign-request, context,
  option-path and origin refusal; time, address-space, output, root depth, node
  and diagnostic budgets; invalid manifests (including lone surrogates), custom
  formats and missing opaque bindings; unrequested metadata; legal multi-field
  output above 1 MiB versus aggregate/individual overflow; actual metadata
  record counts at and over the node budget despite a smaller reported count;
  refusal of result-only, unobserved or missing-metadata success; all three
  metadata facets and priority's independent witness.
- Real Nix checks compare `isDefined` metadata to an independently invoked
  direct Nix Boolean expression with an unselected throwing leaf; import an
  admitted sibling and bound arguments; read a second declared root through its
  pinned `fetchTree`; distinguish a selected throw from a missing input; hide a
  host environment input; deny an undeclared path and an expression outside the
  roots; refuse a hash-pinned loopback fetch before the HTTP server receives a
  request; and reject IFD without a builder marker or lockfile appearing.

These tests establish the exercised runtime controls and projection handoff.
They do not establish general adapter correctness, scalar/path serialization,
string contexts, authenticated source provenance, a production extractor or
queryable combined database. Those need their own slice checks.

## Changing the boundary

Keep F1/F2 authority and the owner-local check import. Add independent failure
and positive controls to the explicit fixture when changing binding admission,
subprocess handling, budgets, publication or evaluator flags. Preserve
successful unrelated requests and health evidence on failures. Format changed
files, run the affected owner checks, and update this note and the existing
registry source list when the abstraction changes. Regenerate instruction
projections through `generate:all`; never edit generated consumers directly.

## Deferred consumers

Increment 4 restores value/member/scalar/string-context validation and fixtures,
including selected-root value success, opaque/empty/null witnesses,
reachability, cycles, shared DAG processing and longest-path depth checks. Their
text and aggregate-output checks remain here on metadata rows. Increment 3
restores nested contexts; the retained transport accepts roots only. E2a
supplies the module adapter and admitted syntax-to-origin links without adding a
value serializer.

<!-- Fragment: packages/codeql-nix/docs/implicit-scope.md -->

# Inheritance and implicit scope

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — N2 extends the lexical resolver with inherited
> declarations, literal `with` members and generated runtime globals.

A binding introduces a name; an occurrence uses it. An implicit scope supplies
names from a `with` environment expression. A candidate is a supported target
for an occurrence. A definite target is established only when no uncertain inner
environment can replace it. This layer extends
[explicit lexical scope](lexical-scope.md) without evaluating Nix values or
adding database tables.

## Inheritance

`Inheritance.qll` contributes through `LexicalScopeProvider`. Both `inherit x;`
and `inherit (expr) x;` introduce static declarations when their containing set
or `let` has an applicable lexical frame. Ordinary sets do not expose inherited
names to sibling values. Inherited declarations participate in the existing
nearest-frame selection and duplicate-binder checks. Known inherited names
suppress same-frame computed-key uncertainty just as ordinary static
declarations do. A frame excluded for a bare inherited occurrence contributes no
uncertainty to that occurrence; unknown membership in other enclosing frames
still applies.

Bare `inherit x;` also makes its name token an occurrence. Lookup excludes its
own declaration frame, so `let x=11; in (rec { inherit x; }).x` copies the outer
`x` rather than referring to itself. The token retains both roles and its
authenticated source location. Plain quoted inherited names use their static
spelling; computed names supply no invented declaration.

In `inherit (expr) x;`, `x` is a selected attribute key, not a variable
occurrence. Variable uses inside `expr` resolve normally, including through the
containing recursive frame. The selected attribute's value is outside this
name-resolution layer.

## Implicit candidates

`ImplicitScopes.qll` supplies fallback candidates through
`ImplicitScopeProvider`. Explicit lexical names always win, regardless of how
deeply a `with` occurs. This includes compatible runtime globals in the
outermost explicit frame. A `with` environment expression is outside its own
implicit scope; only its body receives those names.

For a literal set, static first path components and inherited names establish
membership. Parentheses preserve this recognition. Dotted attributes contribute
their first component as the available name. Repeated contributions choose the
earliest name token as their canonical target. The layer identifies membership,
rather than evaluating member values or proving that the environment evaluates
successfully.

An environment that is not a literal set, or a literal set with a computed first
component, may supply any name. No function, variable, import or computed key is
evaluated to discover members. Such unknown membership is a lookup boundary, not
an enumerated binding for every spelling.

Lookup considers `with` environments from inner to outer. The nearest known
member shadows farther known members. If an unknown environment is nearer, the
retained outer member is only a may candidate; it cannot become definite. With
no supported known member, both target relations are empty. A known member in a
literal environment wins over that same environment's unknown membership.

Source-backed implicit candidates retain their member token's location through
the optional `ImplicitScopeProvider.getDeclaration` method. Its default returns
no declaration, preserving providers whose identities have no location.
`NameBindings.ql` therefore reports a located definite `with` target when one
exists. Its zero target coordinates also cover unavailable resolution and
definite identities without a source location.

## Runtime globals and compatibility

`RuntimeGlobals` connects [generated builtin identities](builtin-models.md) to
N1's `OutermostBuiltinFrameProvider`. Its provider identity is distinct from the
synthetic provider used by the lexical tests, preventing their runtime, model
and symbol facts from combining.

The run's model fingerprint must equal the installed model fingerprint before a
generated global becomes a definite target. Missing or mismatched fingerprints
leave that resolution unavailable. Local declarations still shadow globals. The
raw `globalBindingIdentity` inventory reserves recognized global spellings so an
incompatible global cannot fall through to `with`; inventory membership alone
supplies no compatible-resolution evidence. Runtime identities have no
declaration token or source location.

## Verification and maintenance

`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-anchors` runs the new tests through the existing
F3 owner check. Frozen `NameBindings.ql` and `Resolution.ql` rows under
`ql/test/implicit-scope/` cover inheritance, lexical precedence, known and
unknown environments, locations, and negative controls. Six paired cases
distinguish direct literal interpolation keys such as `${"other"}`, which have
known membership, from parenthesized expressions such as `${("other")}`, which
remain computed in this layer. Their independent expectations preserve both
definite literal-key resolution and uncertainty from computed membership,
including inherited names and excluded frames.
`checks/fixtures/implicit-scope/test_implicit.py` independently evaluates the
source expressions with real Nix, changes unknown membership to reveal capture,
and checks a safe outer rename and an inheritance sentinel.

The same check runs `ql/test/implicit-builtins/` through the installed extractor
for compatible globals, then queries an incompatible model and checks
absent-model rows through the syntax fixture. Nix sentinel values independently
verify global precedence and local shadowing. Synthetic provider tests remain
separate from production identities.

When changing these rules, update independent rows and Nix witnesses together.
Preserve authenticated nodes, inherited binder/use roles,
lexical-before-implicit precedence, must within may, and invalid versus
unavailable. The unknown computed-frame limitations documented in the lexical
contract still apply; this slice makes no general soundness claim for arbitrary
Nix evaluation. Import resolution, value evaluation and builtin-model generation
remain separate responsibilities. Format changed files and run the owner check
through CI.

<!-- Fragment: packages/codeql-nix/docs/installed-extractor.md -->

# Installed Nix extractor

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — P2a installs one coordinator for database
> creation and query tests, preserving authenticated partial work; Q0 adds a
> separate installed lifecycle check; M3 adds the generated model fingerprint to
> the existing run identity. R0 adds production raw-coordinate and
> missing-product lookup controls.

## Terms

- ABI: the shared database tables, identities and text encodings.
- Anchor: a syntax node identified by file, byte range, kind and child path.
- Binding: an explicit map entry resolving an evaluation or argument reference.
- Coordinator: the program that admits sources and joins both producers.
- Discovery: evaluating the project function that declares targets and bindings.
- Extractor: the installed program and schema CodeQL uses to build a database.
- NAR hash: Nix's content hash of a complete directory tree.
- Oracle: an expected answer obtained independently of extraction.
- Pack: a named CodeQL library, query or test directory.
- Producer: a component that emits syntax or evaluation facts.
- Q0: the Step 0 query about which file retains an option definition.
- QL: CodeQL's query language.
- Request: an explicit option path, metadata facet and work limits.
- Run: one extraction identity joining schema, implementation and source
  snapshot.
- Snapshot: admitted source identities, directory hashes and selected file
  digests.
- Target: an explicitly named configuration with bounded requests.
- TRAP: the fact-file format CodeQL imports.

## What installs and why

`lib/packaging.nix` assembles extractor, library and query products. The
extractor's schema and statistics are copied from the library, preserving one
schema for fact import and query compilation. Its `autobuild.sh`,
`index-files.sh` and `qltest.sh` hooks all invoke `src/extract.py` through the
same coordinator launcher. This keeps ordinary database creation and query tests
on the production path.

The recipes under `packages/ai/devTools/` expose the separate products and a
`codeql-nix` command. That command uses the existing CodeQL owner's
`customizePackage` interface to install the Nix extractor and packs beside its
engine. `lib/default.nix` exposes the same packaging function. Pack identities
remain those established by [owner-layout.md](owner-layout.md); the library
retains its own location interface.

## Admission and discovery

Invoke the customized command with
`codeql database create --language=nix --source-root=PROJECT DATABASE`. The
`inputs` extractor option is a JSON map from input name to `{path, narHash}`;
each path must be an absolute directory and match its supplied NAR hash. The
coordinator first copies the project into a private directory and hashes that
stable copy. It excludes only exact CodeQL work-in-progress database, TRAP,
archive and scratch paths supplied by the engine, so query-test output under the
source root cannot change the admitted bytes. Query tests supply the same input
map through `CODEQL_EXTRACTOR_NIX_OPTION_INPUTS`.

The default target file is `.nixql/targets.nix` under the source root. The
`targets` extractor option selects another admitted file; relative paths resolve
under that root. Its `{ inputs, source }: { manifest, bindings }` function
receives pinned local input trees and project source. Discovery uses the
existing evaluation supervisor's offline, restricted, pure Nix invocation and
process controls, with a 60-second deadline, 2048 MiB memory limit and 8 MiB
output limit. Discovery passes its initial directory hashes through
`sourcePins`; the evaluator must match them before constructing pinned local
input trees. Coordinated evaluation requests enforce the same guard. No second
discovery evaluator is introduced.

The result must contain exactly `manifest` and `bindings`, with the manifest
passing the existing [target contract](target-contract.md). Returned copied-tree
paths are restored to admitted paths before request processing; project
evaluation uses the private copy. Syntax retains the original project path for
file and archive identity, checks those bytes against the copied-file digests
and snapshots each file for parsing. Target source roots must match admitted
directory paths. Their content identities and snapshot fingerprints are replaced
with the coordinator's admitted identities; caller labels do not determine the
installed run snapshot.

## One run across both producers

`RunIdentity` in `src/extract.py` owns the shared identity. It hashes the
installed combined schema, producer implementation bytes, admitted root
identities and selected file digests. The generated builtin/module bundle
fingerprint from the packaging pins supplies `nx_runs.modelHash` and
participates in the run key; installed packaging always supplies the actual
model. Legacy fixture pins without a model retain `not-requested`. An explicitly
requested target model must match the run. Named dependency pins participate
even though their syntax is not selected. Only project-root `*.nix` files are
selected for syntax extraction.

The coordinator passes that identity to [syntax extraction](source-identity.md)
and the [evaluation supervisor](evaluation-isolation.md). Syntax checks its
manifest snapshot; evaluation checks target snapshot fingerprints. Each returned
fact collection must pass ABI validation and contain exactly the expected run
row. A foreign run or snapshot is refused. Coordinated children omit their run
row when writing TRAP; the coordinator publishes the sole `nx_runs` row. The
syntax module loads the neighboring coordinator by file path, preserving
callers' module search paths when imported as a standalone driver.

Syntax and evaluation write into temporary staging directories. Authenticated
file/anchor rows and copied-path mappings connect evaluation origins through the
existing [module adapter](module-adapter.md). The supervisor admits
authenticated selected files by exact target root name and content identity
before evaluation, preserving candidates after failed work. Copied-path mappings
retain all file identities; links require exactly one in the target admission
plus trusted provenance and matching original/copied bytes. Explicit labels and
ambiguous aliases leave origins unlinked. Before copying staged archives and
TRAP into CodeQL's destinations, the coordinator validates the combined facts,
recopies the original project with the same exclusions and checks its NAR hash
against the initial private copy. It also rehashes admitted dependencies. A
changed snapshot refuses staged publication, including completed requests from
an otherwise partial run.

Publication copies completed files individually and writes the coordinator run
record afterward. This is no whole-run atomic rename or crash-recovery protocol.
Authenticated partial evaluation preserves completed request facts, per-request
failures and diagnostics, then returns nonzero when a phase is incomplete. Mixed
snapshots or invalid child facts never reach that promotion step. Missing,
throwing, malformed or forbidden-fetch discovery returns failure with a failed
phase and bounded diagnostic. Absent metadata never establishes success.

## Evidence and changes

`checks.nix` imports `checks/installed.nix`, exposing the Linux-only
`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-installed`. Its explicit nonempty runner
executes six installed-path tests, two R0 integration tests and four separate
review-regression tests before writing `$out/evidence`. The installed tests
cover offline language/pack lookup, identical schema bytes, database creation
with syntax and real module metadata under one run, an explicit target file,
query-test extraction, discovery refusals and stale input pins. Direct Nix
evaluation independently checks priority changing from `100` to `50`. Q0 adds
the query-level comparison and failure cases in its separate
[Step 0 check](step0-query.md); that check must pass before claiming the
installed Q0 acceptance contract. The [integration gate](integration-gate.md)
describes R0's independent raw-coordinate rows and missing extractor/library
controls.

The regression suite uses deterministic pin controls for a transient dependency
change during discovery, preservation of completed requests beside failed
requests, refusal to publish partial work after a snapshot change and standalone
syntax-module import. These checks exercise coordinator boundaries with
controlled producers, complementing the installed database tests.

The one-run and stale-pin cases do not independently inject a foreign child
envelope. Keep that distinction when reporting mixed-snapshot coverage. General
evaluator isolation and authenticated syntax mapping retain their separate owner
checks.

Change installation through the existing assembly and recipes, keeping hooks on
the coordinator and schema bytes shared. Change identity or admission through
`RunIdentity` and both producer boundaries, preserving validation and
independent refusal expectations. Register fixtures through the owner check
entry point, format changes and run affected checks through CI. Update this note
and its registry entry when these obligations change.

# Nix language integration gate

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — R0 retires F0 after installed Step 0
> acceptance, promotes its pinned Rust syntax writer into production and
> preserves lookup, exact-text and coordinate proofs in owner checks.

## Purpose and fit

The integration gate now exercises the
[installed extractor](installed-extractor.md) and its separate library,
replacing the disposable syntax/TSV join. Installed
[Step 0 acceptance](step0-query.md) supplies real module metadata and
independent Nix oracles. F0's bootstrap relation, TSV producer, packs, duplicate
queries and check are removed; production checks own their surviving proof
obligations.

`lib/kit.nix` builds the shared Rust implementation from `src/`.
`src/Cargo.toml` and `src/Cargo.lock` preserve the existing vendoring identity;
the Cargo package name `nixql-bootstrap` remains solely to keep pinned
dependency resolution unchanged. The library crate is `nixql_syntax`, called by
`src/anchors.rs` and the raw writer. `src/generate.rs` uses the same inputs for
schema generation. Production assembly continues through `lib/packaging.nix` and
the existing CodeQL owner's engine customization.

## Compatibility pins

- CodeQL CLI: `2.27.3`, asserted by production packaging.
- Grammar: `nix-community/tree-sitter-nix` commit
  `38a15330421d20f3a4d380759f9634d39ba3d8ec`; crate `0.3.0`.
- Kit: `github/codeql` commit `a1575b98a8cc19bcfa7bb6cb41be688cb3dae65c` from
  `codeql-cli/v2.27.3`; crate `codeql-extractor` `0.2.0`.
- Parser runtime: `tree-sitter` `0.26.13` in the committed Cargo lock.

Fixed-output source hashes and the Cargo vendor hash remain in `lib/kit.nix`. An
engine, grammar or kit update requires re-auditing compatibility and all
selected string-emission paths; moving the source does not refresh that audit
automatically.

## Production lookup and coordinate proof

`checks/installed.nix` registers `checks/fixtures/installed/test_r0.py` through
the existing nonempty domain runner in
`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-installed`. The coordinate case creates a
database through the installed coordinator and queries the production generated
syntax and location adapter. Its six independent expected rows preserve
identical `41` tokens in distinct files, a recovered parse and exact
integer-token spans.

The coordinate fixture contains CRLF, a tab and UTF-8 `é` before `73`. One-based
inclusive byte columns place `73` at line 2, columns 27–28 and `97` at line 3,
columns 10–11. The recovered file retains `41` at line 3, columns 10–11. These
rows establish those spans and file identities; the separate
[anchor check](source-identity.md) retains empty-span, ambiguity and broader
source-association coverage.

The negative lookup case invokes the bare engine with an empty search path. It
requires extractor resolution to fail with a diagnostic naming `nix`, and query
compilation to fail naming the missing production library
`nix-agentic-tools/nix-all`. The customized command supplies these products
itself, so it cannot serve as the missing-product control. These checks prove
local missing-product refusal, without claiming a general network fallback
policy.

## Exact text before kit clipping

`src/syntax.rs` checks converted token text and normalized file/folder paths
before the pinned kit can clip tuple strings beyond 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes. The
selected extraction path emits source text through token values; grammar product
tables carry labels and integers. Diagnostic messages also contain paths, so a
bound over the selected kit templates and grammar/schema names first establishes
whether direct extraction is safe.

When the bound cannot guarantee safety, the writer performs private extraction
at a short virtual path, decodes its diagnostic strings and restores the actual
diagnostic path before checking their byte lengths. Only then may real
extraction publish TRAP by rename. This applies to ordinary and recovered trees.
Alternate kit extraction paths and emission changes require a fresh audit.

`src/preflight.rs` exposes `nixql-preflight` over this same production function.
It reads source bytes and a synthetic logical path without creating or archiving
a file at that path. Oversized arguments return exit 2, bounded
`text-field-too-large` stderr and no completed TRAP.

`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-anchors` runs
`checks/fixtures/installed/test_preflight.py` against that production binary.
Its 28 cases cover six token/path categories at 1,048,575, 1,048,576 and
1,048,577 bytes, plus ten parse-error and ordinary-tree diagnostic cases.
Accepted strings must round-trip through decoded real TRAP tuples; oversized
fields must refuse publication. The retired TSV producer's three derived-path
cases disappear with that producer; production evaluation retains its own
transaction validation.

## Changing this gate

Keep integration proofs in the existing installed and anchor checks, with
expected rows independent of extractor output. Change shared Rust code under
`src/`, preserving the Cargo lock and vendoring pins unless intentionally
updating dependencies. Update consumers through `lib/kit.nix` and
`lib/packaging.nix`; keep one production writer and the existing packs.

After changing pins, selected kit emission paths, preflight or location
handling, re-audit exact text and run the affected installed, anchor,
raw-inventory and Step 0 owner checks through CI. Format changed files with
`treefmt` and regenerate scoped instruction projections after changing these
architecture notes. A passing raw coordinate query alone does not replace
installed module-query or authenticated source evidence.

<!-- Fragment: packages/codeql-nix/docs/lexical-scope.md -->

# Explicit lexical scope

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — N1 resolves explicit names through extension
> interfaces consumed by inheritance, implicit names and runtime primitives;
> literal interpolation keys, prefix uncertainty and legacy let scopes are
> explicit.

A binding introduces a name; an occurrence uses one. Lexical scope determines
which binding an occurrence can see from its position in source. A frame is one
group of names visible together. Resolution links an occurrence to a binding. QL
is CodeQL's query language; this meaning layer supplies resolution to
`NameBindings.ql` without evaluating Nix values.

The layer reuses [authenticated syntax](source-identity.md): authentication
checks source bytes against their recorded identity. Only the private bridge
reads generated syntax. `StaticScopes.qll` composes static attributes;
`Bindings.qll` exposes resolution. Static means an identifier, a plain quoted
name or an interpolation whose expression is a plain string without
interpolation, such as `${"x"}`. Its string expression supplies the declaration
location. Other interpolations remain computed; the layer does not evaluate
them.

`let` and recursive sets (`rec`) expose their static names simultaneously,
including inside their own values. Legacy `let { ...; body = ...; }` also
creates a recursive frame and returns its `body` value; it is not a mergeable
literal set. Its declarations shadow outer names. Ordinary sets do not expose
sibling names. Functions expose identifier arguments, named arguments and the
whole-argument name written with `@`; argument defaults can see sibling
arguments. An ellipsis accepts extra arguments without inventing names. Dotted
paths build nested sets; a component becomes lexical only in an applicable
recursive frame. Computed attribute names introduce no lexical binding. Known
path prefixes still determine scope inside computed keys and their values.

Static definitions compose at the same attribute path, including nested paths
and parenthesized sets. A terminal value is a value other than a literal set.
Contributions conflict when either supplies a terminal value at their shared
path; disjoint members merge. Canonical identity is the single target chosen for
a merged name: its earliest name token in source. Conflicts yield invalid
resolution.

Source order also determines recursion: the first creation of each merged set
decides whether it is recursive. A dotted-path prefix first creates an ordinary
set. Later members share the resulting frame; a later `rec` cannot make an
ordinary first creation recursive. For example,
`let c=99; a=rec { b=c; }; a.c=2; in a.b` yields `2`, while placing `a.c=2`
first yields `99`. This prevents choosing a target from source nesting alone.

A recursive frame receiving a computed-key binding, directly or through merged
paths, may bind any name, regardless of whether the value is a scalar, function
or set. Lookup goes from inner frames outward. A known static binding in a frame
wins before that frame's unknown membership, regardless of declaration order.
Until the first uncertain frame, a supported static target is definite. After
that boundary, the nearest supported static target is retained only as a may
candidate; farther static bindings remain shadowed. With no supported candidate,
both target relations are empty. No outer target becomes definite again. A
computed name is never evaluated or invented as a declaration.

An unknown frame is an internal lookup boundary, not a public `Binding` or an
enumerated candidate for every possible name. `StaticScopes.qll` also places
boundaries where computed paths or set contributions may change recursion. Depth
ranks each semantic frame, rather than its composition root: twice the number of
enclosing frames, with possible inserted boundaries between ranks. A computed
contribution at a strict prefix of a recursive frame path makes lookup through
that frame uncertain, even when that frame declares the queried name. This
boundary applies in either source order. A disjoint static key such as
`${"other"}` does not create it. Direct computed keys are evaluated outside
their own recursive set; values have no general exemption.

When an ordinary first contribution suppresses a later recursive frame, a name
declared in that suppressed frame conservatively leaves its outward candidate as
may, never must. This rule is independent of spelling: both `a.${"inner"}={}`
and `a.inner={}` before `a=rec{inner=rec{b=3;probe=b;};}` suppress the inner
recursive frame. With outer `b=99`, Nix returns `99`; the resolver retains that
outer binding as may. A lookup for a name not declared in the suppressed frame
keeps the ordinary static first-creation behavior. This conservative boundary
records the overlap at a declared name rather than inventing a binding for a
frame that does not exist.

`Bindings::Binding` enumerates actual lexical declarations, including unused
ones, and provider identities. A provider contributes semantic facts through a
reserved interface. Keys outside lexical frames, attribute selections and
variable uses are excluded. Lexical bindings have source locations; supplied
identities need not.

The public answers are available as module predicates and occurrence methods:

- `mayResolveTo` returns supported candidates.
- `mustResolveTo` returns a definite candidate only when no competing candidate
  exists; every must answer is also a may answer.
- `resolutionStatus` is `resolved`, `invalid` for conflicting binders, or
  `unavailable` when evidence cannot establish a definite answer.
- `resolutionReason` distinguishes `unique-binding`, `duplicate-binder` and
  `insufficient-evidence`.

Unavailable does not mean undefined or unused. `NameBindings.ql` reports
occurrence locations, status and definite target locations; zero target
coordinates mean no located definite target.

Inheritance copies named attributes; implicit scope supplies names from an
expression. [N2](implicit-scope.md) extends `LexicalScopeProvider` with
declarations and their frames, extra occurrences, and per-occurrence frame
exclusions. Occurrences are authenticated nodes with supported static-name
evidence: native variable uses or nodes selected by this provider. Selected
plain quoted names are allowed; computed names and unselected strings are
excluded. An exclusion starts lookup outside a frame, allowing an inherited name
to refer outward instead of to itself. These contributions use the same
nearest-frame selection, collision checks and identity rules as native
declarations. `ImplicitScopeProvider` supplies fallback candidates only after
explicit names, including the outer runtime frame. The production providers live
in `Inheritance.qll` and `ImplicitScopes.qll`. Source-backed implicit candidates
retain locations through the optional `getDeclaration` method; its default
returns no declaration.

The `OutermostBuiltinFrameProvider` hook admits generated runtime identities
through N2's production provider. Builtins are Nix's runtime-provided
primitives; their outer frame loses to local declarations. A runtime identity
identifies the selected Nix runtime; a model identity identifies the runtime
described by supplied facts. Only matching, nonempty identities admit a definite
builtin target. A missing or mismatched model leaves resolution unavailable; a
recognized builtin with incompatible evidence cannot fall through to an implicit
candidate. N1 provides this hook and synthetic checks; [M3](builtin-models.md)
generates the model. Production and synthetic providers use distinct identities
so their facts cannot combine.

`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-anchors` is the continuous-integration entry
point. It runs reviewed expected rows for scopes, merges, declaration
enumeration and synthetic providers, plus real Nix evaluation and safe-renaming
checks through the nonempty domain-test runner. An oracle is an independently
computed expected answer; the Nix checks provide this separate constraint.

To change resolution, update the appropriate layer and independent expectations
together. Preserve authenticated nodes, canonical merged identities,
explicit-name precedence, must within may, and invalid versus unavailable.
Extend the provider interfaces through their shared selection rules. Format
changed files with `treefmt` and run the owner check through continuous
integration. Imports, value evaluation and builtin-model generation remain
separate responsibilities; inheritance and `with` use the providers described
above.

<!-- Fragment: packages/codeql-nix/docs/literal-imports.md -->

# Literal file imports

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — I2a connects proven builtin import calls to
> admitted literal files through the authenticated source map.

An import site is a call whose function resolves definitely to Nix's builtin
`import`. An import edge links that site to an admitted source file.
`Imports.qll` supplies this static relation; `ImportGraph.ql` reports its sites
and targets. An edge proves a source dependency that syntax and admission
establish. It never says the call ran, the imported value was forced or
evaluation succeeded. Ordinary imports have isolated file scope: caller bindings
do not become declarations in the imported file. Module-collector observations
remain a separate graph.

## Resolve the function first

The library reuses [lexical resolution](lexical-scope.md),
[implicit scope](implicit-scope.md) and
[generated builtin identities](builtin-models.md). A bare `import` must resolve
definitely to the compatible builtin identity. For `builtins.import`, the
namespace variable must resolve definitely to builtin `builtins`, and the
selected member must share the global import identity. Parentheses around calls'
functions and arguments are accepted through the private syntax bridge.

A local function or argument named `import`, or a local `builtins` set, cannot
establish a site from spelling alone. Missing or incompatible model fingerprints
likewise cannot establish builtin import sites. This preserves name precedence
and model compatibility rather than adding a second name resolver.

## Resolve the file through admitted identities

Only a path expression composed entirely of literal path fragments supplies a
candidate. Relative paths start at the importing file's canonical directory
recorded in the [authenticated source map](source-identity.md); absolute paths
supply their own base. Component normalization removes `.` and folds `..`.
Resolution never uses the query process's working directory or searches the live
filesystem.

The map associates each full root/path/content-hash identity with canonical
archived and admitted lexical paths. A target exists only when the normalized
candidate matches either authenticated target spelling. This preserves contained
target symlinks while symlinked sources still use their canonical directory. An
admitted sibling root can therefore supply a target; restricting lookup to the
importing root would lose valid edges. An existing file outside the admitted set
supplies no target. A same-basename file in another directory cannot substitute
for a missing target.

Raw syntax can be shared by logical aliases. Keep the source file argument
correlated throughout `getTargetFile(source)`, `getStatus(source)` and
`getReason(source)`: two files with identical bytes in different directories can
have different relative targets. Full source and target identities remain
available through the file relation; the table query reports relative path
names, which alone do not distinguish roots or hashes.

## Public answers and limits

`Imports::StaticImportSite` represents proven builtin calls, including calls
with unresolved arguments. `getTargetFile(source)` returns admitted literal
targets. `getStatus(source)` is `resolved` when a target exists and
`unavailable` otherwise. `getReason(source)` is empty for resolved sites and
distinguishes:

- `dynamic-path`: the argument has no supported literal path, including
  interpolated paths, strings, variables and search paths.
- `missing-input`: a literal path has no matching admitted target, including
  missing files and files or roots outside the admitted set.

`Imports::importSite` and `ImportGraph.ql` report source path, callee line and
column, status, target path and reason. An unresolved target is an empty string.
Shadowed calls produce no site row.

Directory imports, implicit `default.nix` selection, search-path lookup and
`NIX_PATH` mappings have no resolution semantics in this slice. Neither dynamic
values nor filesystem existence alone justify a target. Generated syntax access
stays inside `RawBridge.qll`; the import layer reuses existing source relations
and adds no evaluation tables.

## Verification and changes

`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-anchors`, explicitly imported by the owner's
`checks.nix`, runs `checks/fixtures/imports/test_imports.py` through the
existing nonempty domain runner. The suite runs frozen
`ql/test/imports/ImportGraph.expected` rows through the installed extractor and
checks the production query separately. It also changes the installed model
fingerprint and requires no inferred sites.

Independent real Nix evaluations cover shadowing, relative paths from a
different process directory, missing files, applied imported functions and
isolated scope. The source-map test checks exact source/target root-path-hash
pairs for aliases, distinct physical bases, sibling and absolute targets, a
basename decoy, interpolation and files outside the admitted set. Its separate
Nix witness arrays expose the values that static admission deliberately leaves
unknown.

When changing resolution, update reviewed expected rows, exact identity
assertions and independent Nix witnesses together. Preserve definite builtin
identity, source correlation and the admission boundary. Extend literal
recognition through the private bridge. Directory or search-path support needs
its own verified evaluator rules and consuming tests. Format changed files with
`treefmt`, run the owner check through CI and update this note when these
obligations change.

# Observed metadata library

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — M3p adds optional retained order to L0
> metadata; M3g adds the observed module occurrence; source properties remain
> separate from observed selection; M3d adds the bounded observed candidate
> inventory.

- QL is the language for querying a CodeQL database.
- A target is an explicitly named configuration.
- A context is a target's root instance.
- A request selects an option path, metadata facet and work limits.
- An observation records an outcome for one typed option, retained definition,
  context, module or definition candidate.
- Selected means retained for type merging, without proving a value's cause.
- An origin is an evaluator label with an optional admitted file or point.
- An anchor identifies syntax by file, byte range, kind and child path.
- A candidate is a literal source binding matching an origin and option path.
- Association quality: zero candidates unmapped, one unique, many ambiguous.
- Priority is the override number, retained as exact signed decimal text.
- TRAP is the fact format imported into a CodeQL database.

`Targets.qll`, `Modules.qll` and `Origin.qll` expose only `Target`,
`RequestResult`, `ObservedOption`, `SelectedDefinition`, `DefinitionCandidate`,
`ModuleOccurrence`, `Origin` and the separate
`PropertyApplication`/`PropertyGroup` structural views. Private
`internal/Evaluation.qll` shares observation witnesses and path encoding over
the [existing tables](database-contract.md). Request results retain failures.

Observed options require their typed subject link and an observed outcome from a
complete or partial request. Selected definitions require their own such link
and an observed parent option in the same request; paths and siblings cannot
supply it. A complete module-graph closure instead observes its context and
every occurrence exactly once, never an option or definition; see
[module-graph.md](module-graph.md). Paths retain exact segments and target
identity. Missing priority stays absent; failed or missing observations
establish neither selection nor a losing definition.
`SelectedDefinition.getOrderPriorityText()` reads optional retained order
independently of override priority; absent order stays absent. The
[module properties query](module-properties.md) returns retained selection rows
only. Structural wrappers use authenticated library formals and generated helper
identities; they can describe inactive source without observed guard truth.

`DefinitionCandidate` exposes the bounded observed
[all-definitions inventory](all-definitions.md), with independent
active/selected states, source anchor, wrapper chain and optional effective
override priority. It is distinct from an origin association candidate; only
authenticated unambiguous retained correspondence links it to a selected
definition.

Origins expose optional file paths and reported UTF-8 byte points. Candidates
reuse [authenticated anchors](source-identity.md), require target admission and
match exact literal paths. Association quality cannot identify the expression
that produced a value. Equal-priority definitions may all remain selected.

The owner's `checks.nix` imports `checks/metadata.nix`, which runs handwritten
`ql/test/step0/Metadata.ql` expectations over independently assembled TRAP.
Cases cover failed/missing work, typed subjects, sparse definition observations,
exact paths, distinct targets, signed endpoints and origin association controls.
Live evaluation needs separate proof. Update accessors and expectations
together; format changes and run `codeql-nix-metadata` through CI.

# Module metadata adapter

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — M3g walks the adapter's module graph into
> observed occurrence rows with exact framed identities, import-tree edges and
> native disabling Booleans; M3d adds bounded candidate plans through upstream
> enabled unique-key collection.

An adapter obtains configuration plus option metadata: a rich result.
`src/eval/nix/adapters/evalModules.nix` takes pinned `lib`, module paths and
JSON arguments; `src/eval/nix/modules.nix` selects one option's metadata without
values. Definitions are retained assignments; declarations introduce options;
origins are file labels; priority is the override number, lower wins. Tied
definitions survive. Every emitted option and retained definition has its own
observation and exactly one typed `nx_observation_options` or
`nx_observation_definitions` link; definition observations identify their
sibling ordinal through the definition entity, never through request text.
`definitions` preserves retained ordinals beside `declarations`, `isDefined` and
`priority`; priority includes `isDefined`. The `selection` facet emits these
retained definitions, whether the option is defined, winning override priority
and explicit order together. It counts option plus definitions, and depth zero
permits only an undefined root option. Order comes from a retained definition's
own `priority` field, stays separate from override priority and remains absent
when upstream omits it. The `module-graph` domain requests the `closure` facet
of a whole-root context: the producer walks the adapter's evaluation graph into
one `nx_modules` occurrence per module, keyed by request, context and zero-based
import-tree path, with `nx_module_roots`/`nx_module_imports` edges, per-node
synthetic or sourced origins, per-occurrence disabling and one observation per
occurrence plus the context witness. Duplicate keys stay distinct occurrences;
the appended argument-support module is reported like any anonymous root. A
runtime rich result without `graph` yields a `graph-unavailable` refusal rather
than an evaluation crash; failed budgets or disabled-import throws yield a
failed request with no graph rows. See
[module-properties.md](module-properties.md) for query semantics. The
[supervisor](evaluation-isolation.md) keeps limits and publication. Callers
supply [S2](source-identity.md) file rows and copy mappings; original and copied
bytes must match before linking. Implicit native module paths retain Nix string
context without changing their label spelling. Plain absolute strings, synthetic
labels, explicit `_file` and explicit definition labels prove no source
identity. The supervisor admits selected authenticated syntax files by exact
target root name and content identity before requests run; unselected files and
failed requests retain this admission. Origin-file links still require trusted
labels plus matching original and copied bytes. Missing rows mean unknown. An
optional pinned `library` descriptor makes this adapter import the actual
library handle; caller-supplied `lib` remains the legacy route without binding
claims. The supervisor supplies independently authenticated top-level function
and `lib` formal candidates, and successful selection and all-definitions
transactions may bind direct root file invocations. `specialArguments.lib`
suppresses these bindings; computed, forwarded and uncovered functions remain
unknown. Library/target/model pins must match. Re-audit lazy label normalization
before value consumers. The `all-definitions` facet adds source-backed
candidates through the same adapter and upstream enabled unique-key collection;
its plan ledger never merges config values. See
[all-definitions.md](all-definitions.md) for source coverage, partial results,
correspondence and collector pin boundaries. Change these producers together,
preserving F1 validation and F2 authorization. Run
`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-modules` for direct Nix comparisons and
refusals; format edits and regenerate through `generate:all`.
