# Observed module graph

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — M3g observes the rich evalModules graph,
> preserving occurrence order, direct disabled flags and atomic completion; F2
> reserves `closure` for graph requests before admission or execution.

## What and why

`ql/queries/DisabledModules.ql` reports every observed module occurrence,
including false disabled flags. Its exact columns are
`(target:text, contextPathJson:text, occurrencePathJson:text, moduleKey:text, originLabel:text, disabled:bool)`.
`Modules::ModuleOccurrence` exposes the reported key, origin, context, target
and Boolean flag; it derives occurrence path JSON from ordered root/import
edges. These are evaluation observations, separate from syntax import edges and
source `disabledModules` expressions. They establish no
declaration-to-disabled-module causal relation.

The producer walks the actual pinned library's rich result `.graph`, whose
collection comes from upstream `collectModules`; it does not reconstruct import
resolution or disabled-key matching. Every exposed root and descendant is
included, even the adapter's appended `{ _module.args = moduleArguments; }`
support root. Internal roots omitted upstream are outside this observation. The
adapter retains its existing authentication and argument injection.

Identity is framed `key("module", [requestID, contextID, occurrencePathJson])`.
The path starts with a zero-based root ordinal, then zero-based import ordinals.
Repeated keys and labels remain distinct occurrences. Root/import list order is
upstream order. `disabled` copies upstream direct membership in its disabled-key
set: a disabled parent's child can be false. It does not describe effective
contributions or final merging. Support-module key collisions retain upstream
behavior; no key is reserved or repaired by the extractor.

Fixture G reports root `[0]` (`root`, `root.nix`, false), children `[0,0]` and
`[0,1]` (both `child`, `child.nix`, true), and support root `[1]` (`:anon-2`,
`<unknown-file>`, false). Removing disabling preserves both child occurrences
with false flags; disabling `root` makes only the root true. Giving the second
child key `other` leaves only the first child disabled. These positions and
support labels are fixture facts, not universal anonymous-key defaults.

## Contract and limits

A request uses domain `module-graph`, facet `closure`, mode `metadata` and
`path=[]`, in the root context only. Capability is `module-graph`. The manifest
schema refuses a graph request with any other facet or a nonempty path before
target admission or execution, and refuses `closure` for `option-metadata`;
discovery rejects multiple graph requests for one context before running
producers; F1 independently enforces request shape and uniqueness on imported
facts. Nested contexts are outside this cut. The supervisor advertises the graph
capability as supported; a rich result without `.graph` returns state `failed`,
reason `graph-unavailable`. This names runtime field absence using the existing
result enum; it does not establish support for every possible library pin.

`nx_modules` holds key, origin and native Boolean flag per occurrence;
`nx_module_roots` and `nx_module_imports` retain contiguous ordinals. Every
occurrence has exactly one root-or-child position and is reachable from roots. A
complete transaction has exactly one observed context witness through
`nx_observation_contexts`, plus one per occurrence through
`nx_observation_modules`, all belonging to that context's closure request. A
context holding module rows must carry that closure request, so these witness
and count checks cannot be skipped by omitting the request. Each observation has
exactly one typed subject. A context witness creates no option observation;
graph requests emit no retained definitions.

`maxNodes` counts the context witness plus every occurrence. Depth counts edges
from a root; `maxDepth=0` permits root leaves. A finite empty exposed graph is
complete with `observedCount=1`; its proof uses independent synthetic protocol
facts because the real adapter appends a support root. Missing rows alone never
prove an empty complete graph or a false flag.

The producer refuses node/depth excess before serialization, preserving
`node-limit`/`depth-limit` instead of a later byte refusal. The supervisor
rechecks graph budgets and applies existing byte, time and memory isolation.
Incomplete closure publishes status/diagnostics without successful observations
or module rows. An imported throw, even below a disabled module, can fail
collection; it must not become empty completion. Cyclic or unbounded import
expansion fails or times out. See
[evaluation-isolation.md](evaluation-isolation.md).

Boolean columns accept only JSON true/false, rejecting integers and strings. The
physical dbscheme uses integer references; TRAP writes `0`/`1` and QL compares
with `1` to expose Booleans. Origins retain reported labels; linking an origin
to source bytes still requires target admission and authentication. See
[database-contract.md](database-contract.md).

## How to change and verify

Keep the existing authorities together: `schema/contract.json` and
`schema/abi.py` define and validate relations; `src/eval/protocol.py` renders
TRAP; `src/eval/nix/modules.nix` emits occurrences; the supervisor authorizes
publication. Update generated schema projections with their existing generator,
then the thin `ql/lib/nix/Modules.qll` and query. Do not change the adapter's
support module to simplify graph expectations. Regenerate instructions through
`devenv tasks run --mode before generate:all` after changing this registered
note. See [module-adapter.md](module-adapter.md).

`checks/fixtures/inc3/graph/oracle.nix` independently invokes `lib.evalModules`
and `lib.modules.collectModules` on original modules with the identical explicit
support module. It imports no extractor or serializer. Installed tests compare
both oracles with query rows, covering repeated keys, root order, path/relative
disabling, support-key collisions, disabled import throws and target isolation.

The existing owner entry `checks.nix` wires Linux `codeql-nix-modules` to
protocol/regression/ownership tests, including typed witnesses, empty
completion, forgeries, uniqueness, budget refusal, malformed-manifest discovery
refusal and module-row closure ownership. Its runner prints
`test_graph_protocol.py: 7 tests, 7 executed`,
`test_graph_regressions.py: 14 tests, 14 executed` and
`test_graph_ownership.py: 9 tests, 9 executed`. The independent O2 regression
prints `test_facet_admission.py: 1 tests, 1 executed`, proving option metadata
cannot use `closure` before admission or execution. The x86_64-linux
`codeql-nix-step0` check runs installed qltests against reviewed expected rows;
find `test_graph.py: 9 tests, 9 executed` and its evidence suffix
`M3g module-graph installed qltest passed`. `codeql-nix-abi` imports native
Booleans through the real schema; `codeql-nix-contracts` covers protocol
sentinels. These are CI entry points and expected log markers, not a claim that
CI has run for this worktree.

# Module properties and retained inputs

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — M3p adds selection metadata, authenticated
> library formals and source property structure through the existing adapter,
> model bundle and database contract; M3r reuses its helper identity for literal
> source rename and alias paths; M3d emits invocation bindings on inventory
> requests too.

## What it answers

`ql/queries/ModuleSelection.ql` reports retained inputs for successful
`option-metadata` requests with facet `selection`. Its columns are target,
context path JSON, option path JSON, selected ordinal, origin label, override
priority and order priority JSON. Paths preserve exact segments. Order is a JSON
string containing signed decimal text, or `null` when upstream supplies no order
field. Ordinals preserve distinct occurrences, including repeated labels.

Selected means retained before type merging and option `apply`. It does not
identify the sole cause of the final value, describe discarded definitions or
explain a custom type's merge. Override priority chooses retained inputs; order
priority sorts those inputs. They remain separate numbers. An origin label can
be synthetic; source association never establishes expression causation.

`Modules::PropertyApplication` separately describes supported source wrappers:
`if`, `merge`, `order` and `override`. It exposes content, condition syntax,
known priority text and the enclosing property. `Modules::PropertyGroup` retains
each literal merge element and its zero-based index. These structures can exist
in inactive code. They establish no observed condition truth and are not rows in
the retained-input query. Unsupported expressions supply no inferred argument or
helper identity.

## How it fits

`src/eval/nix/modules.nix` extends the existing adapter with `selection`. It
reads `definitionsWithLocations`, `isDefined` and `highestPrio`, without reading
merged values or `apply`. Only an explicit retained record's `priority` field
supplies `nx_definition_order`; no default order is invented. Selection emits an
observed option and individually observed definitions. A complete undefined
option has its option witness and no definitions or winning priority. Node
limits count the option plus definitions; root-only depth cannot admit child
definitions. Refusals publish no successful selection transaction. The older
`definitions` facet keeps its existing behavior.

`schema/contract.json` owns both new relations. `nx_definition_order` uses the
existing signed-decimal domain and requires an observed definition.
`nx_module_lib_bindings` links a request to source function/formal anchors and
library/model hashes. F1 validation checks successful request scope, source
admission, structural ownership and target/run fingerprints. The existing
protocol and supervisor carry and validate these facts.

The optional `library` descriptor makes the existing evalModules adapter import
the hash-pinned library root and use that handle for evaluation and injection.
Without it, the legacy caller library remains usable but establishes no binding.
The caller checks the descriptor against the target library hash, common model
bundle and admitted root identity before passing binding candidates. The
supervisor derives candidates from authenticated source bytes and the S2 anchor
tree: a top-level literal function with a formal named `lib`.

The adapter currently covers direct root module-file invocations. It matches
those paths to admitted candidates and suppresses bindings when
`specialArguments.lib` is present. Functions returned by expressions or reached
through another module, and other functions without source anchors, remain
unknown. Missing bindings never prove a function did not execute or used a
different library. Completion covers option metadata, not exhaustive function
coverage. The producer emits bindings on successful `selection` and
`all-definitions` transactions. The [bounded inventory](all-definitions.md)
consumes the same helper identity and keeps its candidate records separate from
retained inputs.

`models/modules/properties.nix` probes helpers and constants from the pinned
library. `models/modules/generate.py` records source export/binding evidence,
helper argument counts, property kinds and priorities, plus the rename argument
roles described in [renames.md](renames.md). Its module fingerprint and the
builtin model fingerprint form one shared bundle identity. `lib/packaging.nix`
installs `models/modules.json` and its mechanical QL projection as
`nix/internal/generated/Modules.qll`.

`Modules::authenticatedLibraryFormal` gates bindings against that generated
bundle. Lexical resolution follows accesses and local aliases from the supplied
formal to modeled exports; local shadowing does not qualify. The single
generated `ModuleModels::helper` predicate binds export identity, kind and
argument specification to both hashes. Source wrappers reuse authenticated AST
nodes; observed selection reuses typed metadata observations. Neither path adds
a second module evaluator or a property fact table.

## Verification and changes

`codeql-nix-step0`, through `checks/step0.nix`, registers
`checks/fixtures/inc3/properties/test_properties.py`. The suite invokes the
installed query, reviewed `ql/test/inc3/properties/ModuleSelection.expected`
rows and direct upstream `oracle.nix` metadata/value witnesses. It covers guard
mutations, repeated merge occurrences, order swaps, override filtering, missing
order and signed endpoints. Separate fixtures exercise aliases, shadowing,
special arguments, the actual injected library, unsupported function shapes,
budget refusals and structural wrapper/group expectations. These are registered
checks, not evidence that a particular run passed. ABI and protocol fixtures
cover relation validation and transport through existing owner checks.

Change helper probes and the shared QL consumer together. Preserve exact pins,
complete application arity, lexical resolution and explicit unknown boundaries.
Extend the existing adapter, contract, transport and supervisor for new
metadata; regenerate schema/model projections with their generators. Keep query
rows independent of structural wrappers and keep real Nix witnesses independent
of the extractor. Format changes with `treefmt`, run affected owner checks
through CI and update this note when recognition or observation boundaries
change.

# Nix CodeQL owner and test entry points

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — M3g retains 32 metadata relations and explicit
> owner check imports; document and check inventories live in the owner registry
> and checks entry point. S1 adds combined-schema generation and standalone raw
> location tests; E1 adds the isolated metadata projection check; S2 registers
> source and anchor acceptance; Q0 adds the installed query check; M3 adds
> generated builtin model acceptance; R0 replaces disposable bootstrap evidence
> with production lookup, coordinate and preflight checks.

## Purpose and fit

`packages/codeql-nix/` owns the Nix language contracts, fixtures and pack
manifests. Its `registry.nix` is the source of scoped architecture documents,
including this note. It contributes through the existing owner registry; no root
owner allowlist or separate discovery mechanism is needed.

`checks.nix` is the source of explicit check imports. Supporting files are not
recursively discovered as checks. Each imported check declares its selected
fixtures, dependencies and platform guards. Add a deliberate owner-local import
when adding a domain, without changing the root flake or copying the inventory
into this document.

## Checks and nonempty evidence

The installed check proves production lookup and raw coordinates alongside the
installed lifecycle; the anchor check exercises shared production text
preflight. The ABI check validates the handwritten schema and independent typed
golden TRAP. The contracts check runs explicitly selected Python suites,
including the manifest/observation boundary, runner behavior and ABI/health
sentinels. The ABI and contracts fixtures alone do not establish production
extraction. Read their imports and commands through `checks.nix` for the current
check and suite inventory.

A check must fail when a selected suite fails and publish its evidence only
after every selected suite passes. Register transport tests in an owner check so
verification does not depend on a manual invocation.

`checks/run-domain-tests.py` accepts one or more explicit unittest file paths.
Each file runs in a separate Python process, with its parent directory available
for companion imports. The runner reports total and executed test counts per
file. Missing files, import errors, failed tests, empty suites, entirely skipped
suites and early `SystemExit` fail the aggregate. It never searches sibling
directories for tests; a passing suite cannot hide an empty later suite.

The ABI sentinel validates the golden graph and compares its relation inventory
with an independently spelled set of all 32 retained relations. The health
sentinel requires runs, targets, syntax results and request results, completed
discovery, successful target/syntax statuses and positive request work counts.
These witnesses prevent empty or failed fixture output from looking like clean
analysis. They validate the fixture contract, not live extraction health or
future evaluator completeness.

`codeql-nix-eval-isolation` adds the Linux-only E1 supervisor fixture through
the same domain runner. Its fake producers and real minimal Nix projections
check serialized metadata requests, budgets, refusal paths and validated TRAP
handoff. See [evaluation-isolation.md](evaluation-isolation.md) for admission
rules, runtime limits and the exact cases. This check supplies no module adapter
or CodeQL database import.

`codeql-nix-builtin-models` adds the Linux-only
[builtin model acceptance](builtin-models.md) through the same explicit imports
and nonempty Python runner. Its suite also invokes its named QL fixtures against
the installed extractor and checks a separate real Nix oracle. Model facts
remain separate from syntax generation and evaluation tables.

## Pack boundaries

Each pack has its own `qlpack.yml` at the reserved interface:

- `ql/lib/`: `nix-agentic-tools/nix-all`, a library selecting `nix.dbscheme` and
  extractor `nix`.
- `ql/queries/`: `nix-agentic-tools/nix-queries`, depending on `nix-all`.
- `ql/test/`: `nix-agentic-tools/nix-tests`, depending on `nix-all` and
  selecting extractor `nix`.

All versions are `0.0.0`; these manifests establish identities. The
[installed extractor](installed-extractor.md) assembles the installed products.
`ql/lib/nix.dbscheme` is a symlink to `../../generated/nix.dbscheme`, S1's
combined generated/handwritten schema. S1's private raw QL and location adapter
supply the library's syntax interface; `codeql-nix-raw-inventory` checks
deterministic generation, inventory drift and standalone generated-node
file/location traversal. S2 adds the syntax driver and private
[authenticated anchor bridge](source-identity.md), tested by
`codeql-nix-anchors` through F3 driver contracts, raw preflight and QL/archive
assertions. The installed extractor, public metadata API and
[Step 0 queries](step0-query.md) now have separate owner checks; Q0 acceptance
requires its installed lifecycle check to pass. R0 removes the disposable
bootstrap packs and check; [integration-gate.md](integration-gate.md) records
their production replacement.

## Adding a domain

Reserve a distinct `ql/test/<domain>/` for each domain's source, `.ql` and
reviewed `.expected` fixtures, and a distinct `checks/fixtures/<domain>/` when
Python or other contract fixtures are needed. Keep those paths disjoint from the
existing `abi`, `contracts`, `eval-isolation`, `installed` and `protocol`
fixtures. A directory reservation does not implement a later capability or make
it a passing test.

Add an owner-local `checks/<domain>.nix` and explicitly import it from
`checks.nix`. For Python contracts, invoke `checks/run-domain-tests.py` with the
exact selected files and declare their dependencies in that check. For QL
fixtures, a domain check must explicitly run the appropriate tests against its
required producer/library; the Python runner does not run CodeQL tests. Preserve
the nonempty guards and independent expectations rather than learning expected
output from the implementation.

Keep shared pack manifests and the ABI coordinated instead of letting domains
rewrite them independently. Change F1 first when relation semantics change;
update F2's independent transport fixtures when that boundary changes. Keep
production extraction acceptance in its installed and Step 0 checks. Format
changed files with `treefmt`, run the affected checks through CI and update this
note when ownership or entry-point obligations change.

# Renamed and aliased options

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — M3r extends the common pinned module-helper
> model and authenticated library-binding path with source rename edges.

## What it answers

M3r recognizes supported source calls to the pinned library's
`mkRenamedOptionModule` and `mkAliasOptionModule`. The first helper forwards an
old option to a new option with a rename warning; the second aliases without
that warning. A rename edge records the helper call and its literal old/new
segment lists. It does not establish that the call executed, became effective or
explains a final value.

`ql/queries/RenamedOptions.ql` returns exactly
`(target, sourceFile, startByte, endByte, helperKind, fromPathJson, toPathJson)`.
Kind is `rename` or `alias`; the byte range identifies the full two-argument
application. Paths are JSON arrays preserving exact segments: `["a.b"]` is one
segment, distinct from `["a","b"]`. Source files must be admitted for that
target. Calls in inactive branches can still be findings.

An empty result is never a complete no-renames answer. Syntax-only extraction,
incompatible models, missing invocation bindings and unsupported source shapes
can all leave recognition unavailable.

## How it fits

`models/modules/properties.nix` probes the two helpers beside M3p's property
helpers. The existing `models/modules/generate.py` verifies source bindings with
the authenticated syntax parser and requires the literal argument names
`from: to:` before recording their positions. Source export/binding evidence,
generator version and the exact library hash remain in
`generated/models/modules.json`. Its mechanical QL projection supplies the same
`ModuleModels::helper` predicate used by properties. The builtin and module
fingerprints still form one shared bundle; changing either model changes that
bundle.

M3r adds no evaluation relation or request facet. It reuses M3p's
`nx_module_lib_bindings`, linking a successful selection request to admitted
function/formal anchors and library/model hashes. The existing adapter imports
the declared pinned library and supplies that actual handle to directly admitted
root module functions. A formal merely named `lib` is insufficient.
`specialArguments.lib` suppresses binding evidence; generated, computed or other
functions without source anchors remain unknown. A fixture requests root
`option-metadata/selection` for `["new"]` to obtain invocation bindings without
module-graph extraction.

`Modules::authenticatedLibraryFormal` checks the common generated fingerprints.
The shared lexical resolver then follows library accesses and proven local
aliases, `inherit (lib) helper;` and outward bare `inherit f;` from a proven
helper alias, while local shadowing blocks recognition. Selections from
arbitrary local or imported records and nested library namespaces remain
unknown; this layer does not resolve record member values.
`Modules::RenamedOption` exposes target, request, helper kind, paths and call
anchor; `Modules::AliasOption` specializes it for aliases. The private syntax
bridge accepts list expressions containing only literal quoted or indented
strings. One shared decoder normalizes quoted escapes and indented-string
indentation and escapes before shared JSON quoting; existing lexical name
consumers retain their fragment-only acceptance guard. Interpolated or computed
path elements, custom `With` helpers and transformed helper paths establish no
edge. This is bounded literal syntax recognition, not a value evaluator.

`rename-models` records exact-pin helper-model availability for each target. A
matching library model is `supported`, a differing pin is `unsupported`, and an
absent model is `unavailable`. This capability can stay supported when a special
library argument prevents recognition. `ExtractionHealth.ql` reports it
separately from authenticated function/formal coverage: positive coverage is
`partial`, never exhaustive; zero coverage is `unavailable`. With no selected
targets it explicitly reports unavailable model and binding evidence.

Existing `Origin.qll` and retained-definition metadata preserve forwarding
origins. An alias edge or equal values do not relocate a destination definition
to the old assignment. The direct oracle independently inspects the
destination's actual `definitionsWithLocations` labels.

## Verification and changes

`checks/step0.nix` registers `checks/fixtures/inc3/renames/test_renames.py`
through the existing nonempty domain-test runner in
`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-step0`. The suite checks frozen
`RenamedOptions.expected` rows and installed queries, helper aliases and
shadowing, exact dotted and multi-segment paths, UTF-8 byte ranges, quoted and
indented escapes, multiline indentation, deferred paths, inactive source,
special-library substitution, incompatible pins, missing capability facts,
synthetic targetless syntax and generated model evidence. `oracle.nix` imports
only the pinned upstream library, independently obtaining values, warnings and
destination labels. The exact R fixture expects forwarding value `7`, a rename
warning and the forwarding module's label; its alias variant expects the same
value without that warning.

CI evidence is each named `test_... ... ok` result and the runner's
`test_renames.py: N tests, N executed` summary. The absent-capability case also
prints
`M3r absent-capability fixture: removed ... capability rows before import`; the
targetless source-only graph is checked with the existing ABI authority and
prints
`M3r targetless syntax fixture: removed ... evaluation facts before import`. The
Q0 and M3p suites share the installed-query runner and retain their own
executed-count summaries. Successful check evaluation alone proves no runtime
assertion.

Change probes, the common generator and shared QL recognition together;
regenerate both model projections instead of editing generated inventories.
Preserve exact pins, complete arity, authenticated source/target association and
explicit unknown boundaries. Extend independent expected rows and direct Nix
witnesses with any new recognized shape. Reuse the adapter, bindings, lexical
resolver and owner check; do not add a rename registry or evaluator. Format
changed files, run the affected owner check through CI and update this note when
recognition or coverage changes.

# Source transactions and syntax anchors

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — S2 authenticates archived source bytes and
> transports the companion anchor index through the existing kit metadata table.
> R0 moves its shared syntax writer and preflight into production `src/`; I2a
> adds admitted lexical target paths to the same source map.

`lib/packaging.nix` exposes
`syntaxDriver/bin/nixql-syntax MANIFEST_JSON OUTPUT_DIRECTORY`. The manifest
supplies roots with `logicalName`, `rootContentIdentity`, `path`, `sourceKind`
and explicit `files` entries containing root-relative `path` and the SHA-256
`contentHash` of admitted bytes. This syntax-only input is separate from the
evaluation target manifest. F1's durable identities retain its existing
root/file/anchor components; SHA-256 authenticates this driver's snapshot
admission without changing the opaque digest ABI.

The driver resolves roots and source paths, refuses escapes through symlinks,
verifies the declared digest and snapshots the bytes privately. The pinned kit
and `src/anchors.rs` both read those snapshot bytes. A second checkout read
after extraction must match before publication. Byte edits change file and
anchor identity. `rootContentIdentity` is caller-supplied; the driver verifies
selected file digests rather than recomputing a digest of the whole root. Equal
text in different physical files remains distinct. Logical aliases of one
resolved path and digest reuse one raw parse and companion index while retaining
each file identity, anchor, metadata index and status. Every alias rechecks
containment and source bytes before cache reuse and publication; raw ambiguity
checks remain unchanged.

Completed raw TRAP is published by rename only after source authentication,
exact-text preflight and F1 transaction validation succeed. Source bytes are
archived under the absolute canonical path with its leading slash removed.
`CODEQL_EXTRACTOR_NIX_TRAP_DIR` and `CODEQL_EXTRACTOR_NIX_SOURCE_ARCHIVE_DIR`
select standard CodeQL publication destinations; otherwise `trap/` and
`archive/` live under the output directory. `facts.json` uses F2's envelope and
contains only F1 relations. Independent completed files survive a refusal. A
failed representable file retains its identity and failed syntax result, with a
bounded enclosing run diagnostic; oversized identity text retains only the
enclosing failure. Source publication is per file, not atomic across a run; the
archive entry is written before the completed TRAP file.

The companion index uses a line-start map over archived UTF-8 bytes. Columns
count bytes: tabs and CR each occupy one column. Raw ends are inclusive; a node
ending immediately after LF ends on the preceding line, including that LF's
column. Empty spans use the kit's start column minus one as the end column.
Anchors retain exclusive byte ends, original grammar kinds and ordered concrete
child-index paths. The index separately records the kit's structural path, which
excludes error/missing children from sibling ordinals and detaches extra tokens.
Pruned nodes retain anchors but have no precise raw association.

`nix/internal/RawBridge.qll` joins authenticated visible F1 identity components
to the raw `File` interface through namespaced `databaseMetadata` entries. It
checks grammar kind, normalized coordinates and the kit structural path before
counting raw candidates. One candidate is `unique`; zero is `unmapped`; multiple
are `ambiguous`. Only a unique association exposes a raw location. Raw labels
are never manufactured, shared with F1 entity types or exposed as durable
identity.

The private metadata keys frame root key, relative path and digest after a
namespaced prefix. `nixql.s2.file|` maps that identity to canonical archived
absolute path, source byte length and admitted absolute lexical path, in that
order. The optional third field retains contained symlink spellings for literal
target lookup; legacy two-field entries still authenticate anchors. Relative
imports use the canonical source directory, while targets may match either
authenticated spelling. `nixql.s2.line|` supplies one-based line numbers and
line-start byte offsets. `nixql.s2.path|` additionally keys the concrete child
path and supplies the kit structural path. Fields escape `%` as `%25` and `|` as
`%7C`, then join with `|`. RawBridge derives normalized coordinates from anchor
bytes and the independent line map; changing an anchor byte span cannot inherit
the original coordinates. Both metadata columns are exact UTF-8 tuple text and
are checked against F1's 1,048,576-byte ceiling before publication. These
entries use the existing generated schema table; S2 adds no handwritten ABI
relation or combined-schema table. They are not evaluation facts or
authenticated evaluator origins. As with every extractor relation, these are
trusted producer evidence; fabricating a file admission record is outside the QL
consumer's archive-authentication boundary. The driver tests establish that
boundary from actual bytes.

The raw writer calls the shared production token, path and diagnostic preflight
in `src/syntax.rs` before calling the kit; added metadata and handwritten facts
receive their own preflight. An oversized field refuses the entire file
transaction with `text-field-too-large`, without raw nodes or anchors from that
file. Re-audit the raw writer when the grammar, kit or selected emission paths
change.

`checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-anchors` registers the driver suite through F3,
inherited raw preflight cases and independent QL/archive acceptance. Keep
expected rows independent of generated output, including duplicate raw
extraction, unauthenticated identities, Unicode/CRLF, empty spans and ends at a
line start. Later AST/evaluation slices must consume this bridge rather than
introduce a second source mapping.

To change this boundary, update the driver, companion index and RawBridge
together, keeping the metadata framing and concrete-to-kit path translation in
agreement. Change F1 first if durable identity or relation semantics change;
regenerate the combined schema through S1 when required. Format changed files
and run `checks.x86_64-linux.codeql-nix-anchors` plus the affected ABI or
raw-inventory check. Keep archive and refusal controls: successful query rows
alone cannot establish that admitted bytes match the source snapshot.

# Target and observation contract

> **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 — F2 retains the metadata manifest and fact
> envelope for Step 0; M3 activates exact-text model identities; M3g adds the
> `module-graph` request domain; M3d adds bounded `all-definitions` requests.

## Purpose and fit

`schema/target-manifest.json` describes explicit named targets and bounded
requests. `schema/observation-protocol.json` carries the resulting F1 facts.
Both use JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. These contracts let future producers and QL
consumers share fixtures before evaluation exists. The
[database contract](database-contract.md) remains authoritative for relation
semantics; the [integration gate](integration-gate.md) records the production
replacement for the retired bootstrap proof.

## Explicit targets

Projects supply `.nixql/targets.nix`, a pure function receiving pinned inputs
and project source. Handles/arguments stay runtime-side; future E1 must bind
each opaque reference to its supplied handle/arguments without inferring from
labels. This JSON boundary specifies no binding-registry implementation and
transports no function or secret values.

The manifest is
`{ "manifestVersion": 1, "targets": { "stable.name": descriptor } }`. Names are
literal labels, never flake attribute selectors. Every descriptor requires:

- `adapter`, `adapterVersion` and explicit `system`.
- `argumentDescription`, containing `hash`, `moduleArgumentsRef` and
  `specialArgumentsRef`.
- `evaluation`, containing `kind` and opaque `reference`.
- `fingerprint`, containing `evaluatorVersion`, `libVersion`, `modelVersion`,
  `policyHash` and `sourceSnapshotHash`.
- Nonempty `inputIdentities` and `sourceRoots`.
- Nonempty `observationModes` and `requests`.
- Boolean `syntaxOnlyFallback`.

The adapter is `evalModules`; accepting a descriptor proves no adapter
implementation. Evaluation kinds are `arguments` and `rich-result`. References
identify admitted runtime handles or arguments; they do not serialize functions
or secrets wholesale. The argument-description hash records the admitted
description. `modelVersion` accepts the same exact-text identity form as the
other fingerprint fields. The installed coordinator requires a requested model
to match its run's generated builtin/module bundle fingerprint, otherwise
returning `unsupported-model`. Legacy `not-requested` remains accepted. See
[builtin-models.md](builtin-models.md) for model generation and compatibility.

Input identities map exact input names to identity strings. Each source root has
`logicalName`, `path` and `rootContentIdentity`. Logical name and content
identity supply F1 root identity; checkout path is mapping data. The fingerprint
fields combine with `adapterVersion`, the argument-description hash and `system`
to supply F1 evaluation-fingerprint components. Validation checks their
representation, not their derivation, source admission, hash authenticity or
runtime-reference resolution.

## Requests and authorization

Every request explicitly provides `domain`, `facet`, literal string-segment
`path`, and all five budgets: `maxBytes`, `maxDepth`, `maxMemoryMiB`, `maxNodes`
and `maxSeconds`. `["a.b"]` and `["a", "b"]` remain distinct. There is no
implicit traversal or value request. The metadata baseline explicitly selects a
prefix.

Every request uses the `metadata` observation mode with the `option-metadata` or
`module-graph` domain. `option-metadata` facets: `all-definitions`,
`declarations`, `definitions`, `isDefined`, `priority`, `selection`. The
[all-definitions inventory](all-definitions.md) emits bounded source candidates
and retained metadata under one request with its own exact-pin capability.
Selection emits retained inputs, whether the option is defined, winning override
priority and explicit order under one request. Its capability is
`module-properties`; unsupported helper pins retain independently requested Step
0 metadata. The `module-graph` domain selects the `closure` facet of a
whole-root context; its capability is `module-graph`, the schema admits only
`closure` with an empty path, a context admits at most one graph request, and an
incomplete closure publishes status and diagnostics only. Objects are closed to
unknown fields; target and input maps permit explicit names.

Deferred surfaces return with their consuming queries: increment 3 restores the
remaining context-parent tables; increment 4 restores
selected-value/member/string-context modes and scalar fixtures; increment 5
restores framework adapters, config-only handles and schema requests. Module
graph requests are restored with the `DisabledModules` query. Other metadata
facets return with the module queries that consume them. The `reusable` cache
control returns in increment 8. Explicit input, argument, root, system and
fingerprint identities remain required now.

## Mandatory validation layers

Consumers must register and enable all three custom formats. A validator that
ignores formats does not enforce this contract:

- `nixql-exact-text`: a string must encode as UTF-8 and occupy at most 1,048,576
  bytes. Character count alone is insufficient.
- `nixql-native-int`: budgets must be native integers in `0..2147483647`,
  excluding Booleans and floats. Parsed JSON `1.0` is rejected even though
  ordinary JSON Schema `integer` accepts it; consumers must retain this
  distinction while decoding.
- `nixql-path`: a path must contain exact string segments, and its compact JSON
  serialization with `ensure_ascii=False` must fit the same UTF-8 byte ceiling,
  including brackets, quotes and escaping.

`checks/fixtures/protocol/test_protocol.py` implements independent format
oracles with Python `jsonschema.FormatChecker`. These are fixture checks, not a
new production validator.

The observation envelope is
`{ "protocolVersion": 1, "facts": [["nx_relation", [arguments]], ...] }`.
Mapping to F1 tables is identity: retain relation names, positional arguments
and values without renaming, coercion or defaults. Each observation carries
exactly one typed subject row through `nx_observation_options`,
`nx_observation_definitions`, `nx_observation_contexts` or
`nx_observation_modules`; text subject fields are removed. The link is mandatory
for every observation state and must remain in its request context and target,
as enforced by F1. The schema checks the envelope and string/array tuple shape.
Then the complete unordered fact collection **must** pass `schema/abi.py`'s
`validate`; envelope acceptance alone is insufficient. F1 owns relation names,
arity, types, identity framing, canonical encodings, references, uniqueness and
scope. Empty facts are representable but cannot serve as a passing extraction
oracle.

## States and exact metadata

Capabilities, phases, targets, request results, observations, syntax results and
diagnostics use their existing F1 relations and separate status vocabularies. A
discovery failure can precede any target. Partial metadata work can record
failed observations without manufacturing a successful result. Missing facts
never imply false or completion.

`text-field-too-large` is an explicit refusal; an affected request cannot claim
completion. Priority transport preserves canonical signed decimal strings over
the F1 signed 64-bit domain, including negative priorities; unsupported range
uses `priority-domain-unsupported`. Native QL integers cannot substitute for
those strings.

These fixtures prove metadata representation and exact text only. They do not
prove authentic source admission, budget enforcement or atomic publication.

## Verification and changes

Run from the repository root in a Python environment containing `jsonschema`:

```bash
python packages/codeql-nix/checks/fixtures/protocol/test_protocol.py
```

The tests check required descriptors, nested source roots and input identities,
retained metadata facets, rejection of deferred controls, literal paths and
budgets, all 36 relation mappings, status families and pre-target failures,
priorities, and UTF-8/JSON-expansion boundaries. They use independent fixtures
and F1 validation without invoking Nix evaluation or the CodeQL engine. F3 must
integrate this standalone entry point into the owner's checks with nonempty
health/ABI sentinels; F2 adds no check registration.

Change the relevant schema and independent fixture expectations together,
preserve all three enabled format checks and the F1 validation layer, then
format changed files and rerun the standalone suite. Update F1 first for
relation or metadata-semantic changes rather than duplicating its validator
here. Update this note when the transport or validation obligations change;
future runtime acceptance must separately establish evaluator isolation and
source admission.
